To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed the inverse scattering theory for integrable type-II field equations, we applied it to massive Thirring model with integrable defect and we derived the defect contributions for number of occupation, the energy and momentum of this model.
we have developed a general method to derive the defect contributions of modified conserved densities of integrable field equations and applied it to the massive Thirting models.
we present an approach to compute the generating function for the defect contributions to the conserved quantities of the integrable massive Thirring model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two topics: 1) The integrability of massive Thirring model in the presence of a type-II defect.
the following topics: (1) The construction of the defect scattering data of integrable field equations associated with the m×m spectral linear problem.
the study of the integrability properties of massive Thirring type models with integrable defects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the defect contributions are not only integrable but also consistent with the underlying field equations.

the defect contribution to the number of occupation and energy of the massive Thiring model with integrable type II defects can be computed by using the inverse scattering approach and the defect contribution to momentum can be computed by the defect contribution to energy and the number of occupation.
the massive Thirting models with integrable defects are integrable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Grassmannian model is integrable for both types of defects, while the bosonic model only for type-II defects.

the defect contribution for the number of particles is given by a sum over a series of modified conserved charges, while the defect contribution for energy is given by a product of a series of modified charges and the momentum defect contribution is given by a series of modified charge products.
the Grassmannian Thirring model is a special case of the bosonic model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the defect contributions for any of the above quantities can be expressed in terms of the defect scattering data.
the defect contributions are independent of the number of components of the field equation.

, in the presence of integrable defects, the generating functions of conserved quantities of integrable field equations are modified in the same way as in the case of integrable quantum field theories.
